rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Biodiversity — genetic, species, and ecosystem levels ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Biodiversity — genetic** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Biodiversity and Conservation fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  **Biodiversity** is the totality of variation in life, measured at three nested levels: **genetic** (variation within a species — rice varieties, dog breeds), **species** (the variety of species in a region) and **ecosystem** (the variety of habitats — Terai grassland, hill forest, alpine meadow).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Three levels with examples: genetic (rice varieties, 50,000+ strains), species (India: ~45,000 plants, 90,000+ animals), ecosystem (forests, wetlands, coral reefs) — one example each.  ·  Trick 2: Latitudinal gradient: species richness ↑ toward the tropics — three hypotheses: speciation time (stable climate), productivity, niche specialisation.

rows.text: **Worked example — one gene that mattered.** In the 1970s, rice crops across Asia were threatened by grassy stunt virus. Breeders screened thousands of varieties and found resistance in one wild relative, *Oryza nivara* — a single population from a single place. That gene now protects millions of hectares.…  ·  ## 7. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Biodiversity is variation at three nested scales — genes, species, ecosystems — and it underwrites every ecosystem service we depend on. **Self-check:** can you place a rice landrace, a tiger and a wetland at their correct levels?
